title: MLA decode with split nope/rope scores
formula: score = (Q_rope @ K_rope^T * scale_rope + Q_nope @ K_nope^T) / sqrt(576); out = E4M3(16 * exp(score - rowmax)) @ K_nope / rowsum, one query row per head over S keys in 256-key tiles; E4M3 [1,H,512] Q_nope and [1,H,64] Q_rope against [1,S,512] K_nope and [1,S,64] K_rope, float32 [1,H,512] out that keeps the 16x probability scale
study_for: The nope/rope split arrives as two separate matmuls and is combined in the VECTOR stage, not by concatenating features: grep `scale_add_qk_vf` in kernel.py — `(rope * scale_rope + nope) * SCALE`, where `scale_rope` is a per-batch runtime value read from GM. `SCALE` itself is `1/sqrt(Dn + Dr)`, taken over the combined width.
The E4M3 carriers are split too: `q_nope`/`k_nope` are Dn=512 wide and `q_rope`/`k_rope` are Dr=64, so the two products have very different K depths and are not interchangeable tiles.

K_nope is both the key and the value matrix: one `l1kn` tile feeds the QK matmul and then, transposed, the PV matmul of the same iteration (`matmul(l0cpv[...], l1p[...], l1kn[...].T, splitn=128)`). The tile is loaded once and its double-buffer slot is what ties the two stages' depths together.
do_not_copy_when: Your rope scale is a compile-time constant. Here it is a GM input per batch, and folding it into `SCALE` would change the ABI.

You need the normalized attention output. The 16x probability headroom is deliberately never divided back out — `E4M3(16 * P)` multiplies V while the denominator is the unscaled FP32 sum — so this kernel's result is 16 times the attention, by the source's convention, and the reference reproduces that rather than correcting it.

Your batch is larger than one or your key count is not a multiple of 256. The body addresses batch 0 (`q_nope[0, ...]`) and every key tile is a full BASES tile: there is no tail path here at all, unlike attention.a5_decode_fp8.
